record_type_quote: In a large sample of twins oversampled for language problems, the present study failed to find evidence for atypical laterality, either in terms of handedness or cerebral lateralisation for language, in those with DLD.

targets.title: Atypical cerebral lateralisation in adults with compensated developmental dyslexia demonstrated using functional transcranial Doppler ultrasound
targets.evidence_quote: Theories have proposed that disruption to the typical left hemisphere dominance for language may be a neurobiological correlate of language problems (e.g., Annett, 2002; Bishop, 2013; Crow et al., 1998), and empirical studies of very small samples have supported that view (Illingworth & Bishop, 2009; Whitehouse & Bishop, 2008). However, the present study did not replicate these findings, and we suggest that they are likely to have been false positives.

targets.title: Does cerebral lateralization develop? A study using functional transcranial Doppler ultrasound assessing lateralization for language production and visuospatial memory
targets.evidence_quote: In the second step of analysis, we tested the relationship between language and laterality from the opposite direction, using language measures as predictors, aiming to replicate the effects reported by Groen et al. (2012). We computed Spearman’s correlations between each language measure and the fTCD laterality index in the two replication samples. However, no uncorrected correlation replicated across samples, and no correlation within a sample survived a Holm-Bonferroni correction.
